purpose.primary: Provide the machine-readable index and interpretation contract for the optional Lean 4 formal companions used by 5Guides.
purpose.educational: Use small formal examples to make definitions, assumptions, relationships, proof obligations, and formalization boundaries inspectable.
purpose.principle: Formal methods can make reasoning explicit. They do not remove the need to inspect what was modeled.

groups.role: Formal companions for the five AACCC Guides.
Small formal teaching abstractions derived from selected project-lineage materials.

guide_companions.name: Awareness
guide_companions.question: What am I observing?
guide_companions.formal_focus: Inspect variables, types, hypotheses, and the goal before attempting a proof.
guide_companions.educational_role: Make the formal observation state explicit.

guide_companions.name: Alignment
guide_companions.question: What corresponds?
guide_companions.formal_focus: Use explicitly established equality or correspondence to justify transformation.
guide_companions.educational_role: Show that formal substitution depends on a declared or proven relationship.

guide_companions.name: Coherence
guide_companions.question: Does this hold together?
guide_companions.formal_focus: Inspect whether a conclusion follows from the supplied definitions and assumptions.
guide_companions.educational_role: Make unsupported formal conclusions and missing assumptions visible.

guide_companions.name: Clarity
guide_companions.question: Can this be understood and inspected?
guide_companions.formal_focus: Compare proof representations that preserve the same result while exposing different amounts of intermediate structure.

guide_companions.name: Continuity
guide_companions.question: What persists through change?
guide_companions.formal_focus: Inspect how formal structures and proved relationships behave when definitions, values, or transformations change.
guide_companions.educational_role: Make persistence and proof breakage under change inspectable.

origin_companions.name: TFT Origin
origin_companions.formal_focus: Generic three-position structure and component-wise transformation.

origin_companions.name: Nawderian Theorem
origin_companions.formal_focus: Explicit dimension-group membership and selected intersection relationships.
origin_companions.source_scope: Relationships directly supported by declared group membership.

origin_companions.name: Nawderian SET Theorem
origin_companions.formal_focus: Named additive contributions and their modeled total.
origin_companions.source_scope: Small algebraic teaching abstraction of the declared contribution structure.

origin_companions.name: Temperature Engine Theorem
origin_companions.formal_focus: One-dimensional signed relation and selected zero and sign properties.

origin_companions.name: Unified Resonance Theorem
origin_companions.formal_focus: Explicit local algebraic assumptions supporting a three-factor composition.
origin_companions.source_scope: Teaching algebra introduced to expose required assumptions.

origin_companions.name: RTT Origin
origin_companions.formal_focus: Small integer-valued state and update model.

compiler_validation.scope: The human-source Lean teaching artifacts in docs/5Guides/lean.
compiler_validation.meaning: Lean accepted the represented formal artifacts under the stated compiler environment.
does_not_mean: The broader source frameworks were empirically validated.
Every source interpretation was fully formalized.
The teaching abstractions are complete models of their source concepts.

prefer: Lean accepted the formal artifact under the stated environment
verified consequence of the supplied formal definitions and assumptions
avoid: Lean scientifically validated the source framework
The compiler proved the physical interpretation

formalization_contract.formal_question: Given these definitions and assumptions, does the conclusion follow?
formalization_contract.modeling_question: Do these definitions and assumptions represent what we intended to describe?
formalization_contract.empirical_question: Does the model adequately describe the relevant real-world evidence?

artifact_contract.principle: An AI-facing Lean artifact should expose enough structure to distinguish source interpretation from formal consequence.

questions: What came directly from the source?
What relationship is actually being proved?
source_alignment.principle: The formal artifact should not float free from the concept it is intended to represent.

assumptions.principle: Assumptions remain part of the meaning of a formal theorem.
assumptions.avoid: Report only the conclusion while hiding materially relevant assumptions.

undefined_semantics.principle: If the source does not define a relationship precisely enough to formalize, preserve the gap.
undefined_semantics.avoid: Invent a convenient relation merely to make a desired theorem pass.
undefined_semantics.preferred: Identify the relation as requiring definition before stronger formal claims are made.

possible_causes: theorem does not follow from supplied structure
formal model does not represent the intended concept
preferred_response: identify what changed or is missing
decide whether the proof, theorem, assumption, or model needs revision
proof_failure.avoid: Change the theorem merely to make the compiler green without inspecting whether the meaning changed.

proof_success.principle: Compiler success is necessary evidence for a claimed Lean proof under the stated environment but is not sufficient evidence of good modeling.
questions_after_success: Does the formal object still correspond to the intended concept?
Did any added assumption become hidden?
Does the result remain inside the claimed formalization boundary?

awareness.formal_habit: Read the variables, types, hypotheses, and goal before proving.
awareness.question: What has actually been declared?

alignment.formal_habit: Use only established relationships to justify substitution or mapping.
alignment.question: What formal relationship permits this transformation?

coherence.formal_habit: Check whether the conclusion follows from the formal context.
coherence.question: Does this theorem actually follow?

clarity.formal_habit: Choose a proof representation that exposes the structure relevant to the learner.
clarity.question: Can the proof be inspected?

continuity.formal_habit: Change a definition, value, assumption, or transformation and inspect what survives.
continuity.question: Which formal relationships persist through change?

alignment: Which formal object corresponds to which source concept?
coherence: Do the definitions and assumptions support the theorem?
Does the proof actually close the stated goal?
clarity: Are source claims, formal definitions, assumptions, and verified consequences distinguishable?
Can the proof structure be explained in plain language?
continuity: What changes if a definition, assumption, value, or type changes?
Did semantic meaning drift even if code still compiles?

formal_vs_explanatory_clarity.formal_clarity: Exact definitions, types, assumptions, theorem statements, and proofs.
formal_vs_explanatory_clarity.explanatory_clarity: A learner-readable explanation of what those formal objects mean and why they matter.
formal_vs_explanatory_clarity.principle: Exactness does not eliminate the need for understandable explanation.

types_as_modeling.principle: Type choice participates in the formal model.
questions: What values must the model represent?
Would another type preserve more of the intended structure?
Did only the implementation environment change?

compiler_vs_semantic_continuity.semantic_continuity: The artifact continues to express the same intended meaning.
compiler_vs_semantic_continuity.warning: A theorem may continue compiling after a definition changes while representing a different claim.

student_questions: What did the formal file define?
What does the theorem actually claim?
What would have to change to model more of the source?

reproducibility.principle: Another person should be able to identify what formal artifact was actually checked.

origin_boundaries.06_tft_origin: Generic triad properties do not validate TFT's broader physical proposals.
origin_boundaries.07_nawderian_theorem: Membership proofs do not define the source term wrapping.
origin_boundaries.08_nawderian_set_theorem: Additive teaching structure does not establish physical completeness.
origin_boundaries.09_temperature_engine_theorem: Signed algebraic properties do not validate the broader physical interpretation.
origin_boundaries.10_unified_resonance_theorem: Local algebraic assumptions do not establish that source factors naturally form that algebra.
origin_boundaries.11_rtt_origin: Small state-transition properties do not formalize or validate the complete RTT specification.

must: Treat Lean as an optional formal companion.
Preserve the distinction between guide companions and origin companions.
Report compiler validation at the scope actually checked.
Expose assumptions and definitions before interpreting theorem results.
Treat proof failure as potentially informative.
Recheck semantic correspondence after formal revisions.
must_not: present compiler success as empirical validation
present origin teaching abstractions as complete source formalizations
invent source semantics to satisfy a proof
change theorem meaning solely to obtain a green compiler result
treat AI-generated Lean as verified before compilation
assume continued compilation guarantees unchanged meaning

do_not_infer: current compiler compatibility outside the stated validation environment
